title: llama.cpp server
description: The agent works with a model on your llama.cpp server instead of the cloud: only the server's address is opened, nothing else.

llm.label: llama.cpp server (sandbox-ai llm list), NAME or NAME:MODEL
llm.hint: sandbox-ai llm add llamacpp --kind llamacpp --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --model MODEL

notes: Register it once: sandbox-ai llm add llamacpp --kind llamacpp --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 (another address, --api-key-secret SECRET for a key, --vpn PROFILE for a server behind a VPN).
Start it with: llama-server -m MODEL.gguf --jinja -c 32768 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 (--jinja for tool calls).
OpenCode works with any llama-server; Codex needs b7793 or later (b9161 for Codex's tool types), Claude Code b7187 or later (Anthropic Messages API).

NAME:MODEL picks a model (sandbox-ai llm models NAME lists them); without it the server's default (llm add --model) or its only one. sandbox-ai llm check NAME --agent AGENT asks the server whether it has the API that agent needs.

On this host's loopback (http://127.0.0.1:PORT) only with Podman: sandbox-ai opens that one port for the sandbox, and the server must listen on 127.0.0.1. In your LAN or tailnet: a private address, or https.
The agent reaches nothing but the server (--no-provider-defaults): no cloud provider, its login is not copied in; the server's key stays with the connection proxy.
